intro: Aihole is a village in Bagalkot district in northern Karnataka, scattered with more than a hundred stone temples from the Chalukya centuries, many of them in ruins. On the ground of the Galaganatha group, by the Malaprabha river, grows a fig whose crown spreads far wider than it is tall, a stone Nandi lying beside it. A reader sent us its photograph.

trees.name: The Galaganatha Temple Fig

location.address: Galaganatha group of temples, Aihole, Bagalkot district, Karnataka

trees.story:
A reader walking among the temple ruins of Aihole, in northern Karnataka, sent us this tree and placed it on the ground of the Galaganatha group, the cluster of old Shiva shrines on the bank of the Malaprabha river that the Archaeological Survey of India protects as a monument of national importance.

Their first photograph shows why they stopped. Across a stretch of bare red earth the tree spreads into a low, even dome of green many times wider than it is tall, the kind of shade a whole village could sit in. Walk closer and the crown turns out to stand on a short, fluted trunk that breaks almost at once into a dozen grey limbs, reaching out level in every direction, a few thin aerial roots hanging from them. A carved stone Nandi, Shiva's bull, lies on a plinth beside it, facing the tree.

The reader knows it as an Indian banyan. The leaves, the small red figs and the hanging roots say fig; which one, we would like a reader to confirm. We have no age, girth or story for it yet. If you know what the people of Aihole say about this tree, tell us here.

Come early, as the reader did, and stand in the middle of the shade looking up into the limbs.
